questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I personally wanted to travel to southern Germany because of the nature and landscape along with the weather. The fact that Heidelberg has the oldest university in Germany was also a plus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All in all I had a very nice experience. I have made friends, that I still keep in contact with. I also got to explore new cultures and travel a lot due to the flexibility of the exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy, there was just a lot of practical things that had to be done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were each assigned a buddy by the University of Heidelberg, if we had any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found housing on my own on
wg-gesucht.de
, which usually is quite hard and takes a long time. I, however, was very lucky that one out of the first five ads I responded to replied.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you can't really live on campus in Heidelberg anyway.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a long process, and in Germany a lot of things has to happen in person which can be quite annoying.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First of all you have to register as a citizen at the city hall. Then you have to send copies of personal information and your lease (I believe) to your host institution. Then you go and pick up your new student ID.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In terms of the registration process I don't know. I didn't seek any.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to stay updated with any deadlines. And start well in advance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course levels were very comprehensible even as an exchange student. The teachers were very understandable in terms of us being exchange students. They are after all used to it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more teaching in plenum in Germany than at UCPH. Hardly any group work, mores presentations and moderations and tests. And more written assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Aussteigen in Literatur und Film der Gegenwart
Medienikonen: die Inszenierung und Kanonisierung von Bildern als visuelle Erinnerungsorte 
Wissenschaftlichen Arbeitens

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend courses that aren't too difficult and too different from what you have already worked with. It's going to be more difficult due to everyone speaking fluent German anyway so you might as well have that advantage.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It wasn't really unexpected but I did rent a Swapfiets for six months.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were a lot cheaper in Germany than in Copenhagen. Train tickets were a bit more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could sign up for pretty much every sport possible via the university. I signed up for tennis and really enjoyed it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for a sport! Great opportunity to meet new people and get some fresh air and exercise.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel. Heidelberg is located great, there is a lot of opportunities to go see other cities such as Frankfurt, Tübingen and even travel to France.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy actually.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to make mistakes when talking to locals. Sign up for sports or any other activities that the host university is offering.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing comes to mind right now.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy it while it lasts, the times goes by so fast. 
Don't get run down because of all the practical things in the beginning that needs to be done. You will get over it.
Travel around southern Germany, it has a lot to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend some Erasmus events at the beginning. Great way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends and bettering my German skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making new friends and bettering my German skills.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
